thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: P2 - Elevated generation latency observed for hosted inference (us-west-2). 50% requests > 1200ms over last 5m. Auto-page: alex_oncall, maya_sre.

alex_oncall: I’m on it. Initial check: no recent config changes from self-serve. Looking at runtime metrics and recent deploys.

maya_sre: I see a spike in tail latency on the L1 serving node pool starting at 10:14 UTC. Throughput steady. Error rate normal.

jon_ml: throwing in a hypothesis—we landed a kernel selection change in eng-runtime two nights ago that could change per-token compute path. Could cause slowdown for long context.

alex_oncall: noted. timeline: 10:08 normal; 10:12 latency climb begins; 10:14 alert. Starting timeline capture.

lina_prod: customer_ops reports a handful of customers with UX timeouts in the console, some retrying. @customer_ops please collect customer IDs impacted.

customer_ops: sending list via DM to Lina. Two enterprise customers reported timeouts, both using long-context chat flows.

maya_sre: gathering logs from pods in us-west-2: `kubectl -n prod logs -l app=inference -f --since=15m` — attaching clipped tail: ```
[10:13:12] request_id=abc123 seq_len=1024 token_ms=48 total_ms=1285
[10:13:13] request_id=def456 seq_len=2048 token_ms=52 total_ms=2150
[10:13:14] request_id=ghi789 seq_len=512 token_ms=51 total_ms=430
```
Noticing per-request `total_ms` correlates with sequence length. Token_ms not hugely different. Looks like aggregation or KV cache miss for large seqs.

jon_ml: Important: we merged a change to KV-cache shard sizing in the optimization branch yesterday. If large prefixes aren't hitting cache, assemble time balloons. Hypothesis A: KV cache sizing/regime change -> cache misses for long contexts. Hypothesis B: new kernel path slower for > 1024 tokens (per-job code path regression).

alex_oncall: Plan: 1) Scoped rollback test of runtime image to previous release in a single canary pod. 2) Temporarily pin long-context customers to fallback model variant (shorter effective context) via routing rule. 3) Run targeted load test against canary.

maya_sre: Assigning owners: runtime revert canary -> @alex_oncall; routing pin -> @lina_prod (with customer_ops); load test -> @jon_ml.

devops-bot: @alex_oncall triggered rollout: `k rollout undo deploy/inference-runtime -n prod --to-revision=42` (canary-1). Watch: `k rollout status deploy/inference-runtime -n prod`.

alex_oncall: canary rolled out. Attaching probe logs from canary with identical test requests (seq=2048): ```
# canary (rev 42)
[10:30:01] request_id=test1 seq_len=2048 total_ms=680
# prod (rev 44)
[10:30:01] request_id=test1 seq_len=2048 total_ms=2200
```
This is promising — older revision shows much lower latency for long seq.

lina_prod: Pinned routing for affected customers: `route set --customer CUST123 --model redwood-legacy-ctx2k --until 2026-03-15T12:00Z` Done for both reported enterprises. Confirmed via routing logs: `routed customer=CUST123 model=redwood-legacy-ctx2k`.

customer_ops: Customers notified with temporary mitigation and ETA for full fix. No new customer outages reported after pin.

jon_ml: Running controlled load test against canary and prod (ab-level): ```bash
# simple gen test
python tools/bench_gen.py --seq 2048 --rps 5 --duration 120 --target canary.us-west-2
```
Results: canary mean=650ms p95=920ms, prod mean=1980ms p95=2400ms. Clear regression in current prod image.

maya_sre: Elevating hypothesis priority: runtime change (merged in PR #2345) is likely root cause. Need rollback of the runtime release.

alex_oncall: Caveat: we changed both kernel selection and KV-cache sizing in that PR. We should test reverting each individually if possible, but immediate customer mitigation suggests full rollback of the release is quickest.

lina_prod: Business decision: roll back runtime prod to rev 42 across us-west-2. Notify customers about potential brief capacity blip. Approved.

devops-bot: Scheduling rolling restart: `k set image deploy/inference-runtime redwood/runtime:rev42 -n prod --record` — rolling update across node-pools with maxSurge=1.

maya_sre: Monitoring: token-level latency traces show p95 for long-context requests dropping to <1s as pods on rev42 come up. No error spikes.

jon_ml: Post-rollback diagnostics: we'll create two isolated experiments in staging: (A) only revert the KV-cache sizing; (B) only revert kernel selection logic. We need perf traces for both to determine which sub-change caused regression. Assigning: jon_ml owns experiment A, maya_sre owns experiment B.

alex_oncall: Can we capture flamegraphs/trace spans for the long requests on both variants? Add `X-Debug-Trace: perf` header in test harness to get profiles.

jon_ml: Already captured traces from both images. Attaching summarized diffs: `kernel_time_avg: prod=320ms, rev42=110ms; cache_lookup_ms: prod=22ms, rev42=24ms`. That indicates kernel path is the bigger contributor.

lina_prod: Good diagnostic. Action plan: 1) Keep revoked runtime (rev42) in prod. 2) Reopen PR #2345 for a smaller diffset (split kernel path change out) and perform more perf regression tests across sequence lengths before re-landing. 3) Notify customers of rollback and planned follow-up.

alex_oncall: Creating incident timeline entry in the RCA doc (internal): "10:12 UTC - latency spike; 10:30-10:40 canary rollback -> p95 improvement; 10:45 rolling rollback across us-west-2; 11:05 customer pins applied; 11:30 monitoring confirms stabilization."

maya_sre: Root-cause hypothesis for RCA draft: "Regression introduced by kernel selection optimization in PR #2345 that increases per-token kernel overhead for long-sequence generation, causing p95 tail latency regressions for requests >1024 tokens." Marking as "hypothesis (primary)".

jon_ml: Secondary hypothesis: KV-cache sizing change may exacerbate misses for some patterns, keeping as "hypothesis (secondary)" pending experiments.

lina_prod: Postmortem action items (owners): - Split PR #2345 into kernel-only and cache-only (jon_ml). - Add perf gate for seq lengths {512,1024,2048} in CI (eng-infra). - Add automatic routing fallback for customers on long-context heavy flows (product). - Improve release notes to call out perf risk for long-context changes (eng-releases).

alex_oncall: Will keep on-call shift updated. Leaving this thread open for RCA coordination. If someone wants to pick up the postmortem write-up, ping me.

customer_ops: customers acknowledged rollback and appreciated rapid mitigation. One asked for a timeline — we provided ETA for fix cadence.

devops-bot: Rollout complete across us-west-2. All pods image=rev42.

maya_sre: Last check: 60m after rollback, p95 for long-context requests stabilized ~850ms, traffic back to normal. Closing active paging.

alex_oncall: Closing notes: immediate mitigation = rollback; next steps = isolate kernel change and re-benchmark; timeline added to RCA doc. Thanks all. :handshake:

incident-bot: Incident P2 resolved (latency) — thread archived.
